Native combat report construction, DF 53.16 configured Windows PEs
================================================================

Source extraction: tools/extract_combat_announcement_sources.py and
tools/DecompileCombatAnnouncements.java.
The configured reference and classic images were read and disassembled locally;
the manifest owners were then decompiled from those same original PE bytes by
Ghidra 12.1.4 into real per-owner C. There are 41 logical native owners per image,
82 .c files in total, each beside its corresponding .asm. This document describes
their production grammar; it is not a substitute for the original-PE C exports.
Image identities: reference PE:6a70a6d9:02711000; classic PE:6a70b91c:0270a000.
This is static source extraction, not observed game output. The extractor
never executes the game, a translation, a generator, or a build. Addresses below
are reference native VAs; native-owners.tsv retains the independent classic VAs.
PE CHAININFO merges unwind pieces into complete logical native functions.
Each .c header retains edition, PE identity, role and logical owner boundaries.
The C keeps Ghidra's original diagnostics and inferred types; these are recovered
source expressions, not original developer variable names or complete C++ types.
Native selector destinations are supplied from native-switches.tsv, and complete
unwind owner boundaries prevent tail transfers from swallowing unrelated owners.
The 2026-10-18 shot/defense follow-up re-decompiles the complete melee/projectile,
item-caption, unit-caption and body-part owners directly from both configured
PEs, using the same DecompileCombatAnnouncements.java and their retained native
owner/call/literal/selector operands. These are complete owner C exports, not
just the string sites shown by the screenshots. The other existing owner C
exports remain the source graph for shared damage, projectiles and item subtypes.
The std::basic_string overflow throw is nonreturning at reference 0x140065890 and
classic 0x140065820; the selector bytes following that call are data, not extra
English productions or reachable x86 instruction branches.
Each per-owner .asm retains the decoded owner bytes, including non-text operations
and embedded selector data that linear disassembly can render as instructions;
native-control-flow.tsv retains conditions and branches; native-calls.tsv retains
direct calls/tail transfers; native-switches.tsv retains decoded case/default
paths; native-literals.tsv retains RIP strings, vector operands, inline stores.
Printable numeric immediates such as division constants gfff/VUUU and integer
argument 0x32 are source operands, not caption vocabulary. Text production below
is reconstructed by following string assign/append calls and string stores.

Announcement transport and display consumers
-------------------------------------------
Reference / classic pairs, both with real PE C and assembly in this directory:
  announcement submit:       0x1400e3c20 / 0x1400e3bb0
  popup render:              0x1400e9f40 / 0x1400e9ed0
  adventure row construction:0x1408a40e0 / 0x1408a1960

The submit function takes the complete text as its second argument, validates the
announcement type (0..0x163), applies native visibility and per-type routing flags,
and copies that complete string together with color and announcement metadata.
It does not choose a finite vocabulary for the names, body parts, items or speech
inside the string. Existing report matching may increment its repeat count and
refresh its lifetime; otherwise a new report receives the full submitted text.
Its local Empty announcement diagnostic is error-log text, not a normal message
to translate into the battle panel. Sound, location and ownership bookkeeping
are preserved in C but are not additional English caption fragments.

The popup renderer consumes already constructed entries at object+0x48..+0x50,
copies each entry's three color bytes (+0x20..+0x22), and uses its native x/y
coordinates (+0x28/+0x2c). The portrait-present branch shifts the text origin
from +2 to +0xe and widens the frame. Its only direct English control labels are
Okay (one queued page) and More (multiple queued pages), stored as immediates.
The renderer neither reconstructs actor names nor translates report contents.
The adventure row builder consumes report.text at +8: strings shorter than 0x60
are used whole; longer strings are passed to the existing 0x5f-width splitter.
Each resulting row retains its originating report pointer. Color, wrapping,
portrait layout and report lifetime are display branches, not alternative combat
verbs. Complete sentence translation must therefore happen before the native
wrapped fragments lose their full sentence and dynamic-field ownership context.

The rendered panel accepts other producers using the same announcement transport.
The 41-owner combat/source manifest is a scoped construction tree and includes
its display consumers and complete corpse/body/material suppliers; it is not
a claim that this UI admits only 41 producers.
The broader announcement-popup-native transport/catalog extraction and existing
status/death/speech source extractions retain those additional producer families.

Complete typed dynamic input fields
----------------------------------
UNIT = complete native unit caption (0x14132e430), including player You, names,
       identities, complete creature/caste descriptions and complete professions.
OWNER = Your / UNIT + "'s" / native possessive pronoun your/his/her/its.
BODY = complete body-name formatter (0x1413345d0) or indicated inline RAW name.
LAYER = complete body/tissue/material field, optionally BODY + "'s " + TISSUE.
ITEM = complete native item caption (0x140c65450), preserving inner title,
       material, subtype, artwork subject and outer native quality/wear markers.
MATERIAL = complete native material/state name, optionally native creature owner.
Generated and authored identity/name fields are not finite English word lists.
They remain open dynamic fields even after every finite branch is decompiled;
the installed RAW rows describe available inputs, not all future world/mod text.
Authored names must retain their source identity and original spelling. A field's
spelling alone cannot classify it as authored, generated, a creature descriptor,
a profession, an item title or a custom squad alias.
A caption such as +larch figurine of blood gnats+ is one ITEM with quality markers,
wood material and figure subject, not an English word substituted in isolation.

Recovered identity and speech field suppliers
--------------------------------------------
UNIT: reference-132e430.c / classic-13293a0.c. Branches include adventure-player
You/you, identity/name selection, complete creature/caste and profession fields,
appearance, articles, slave/prisoner, agitated/fierce/stray, corpse/ghost and the
native force/deity fallbacks. These complete fields cannot be split into a final
word guessed to be the profession. The screenshot's multiword creature identity
and worshipper-of-change profession remain separate native input components.
ROLE: reference-132f980.c / classic-132a8f0.c, with independently decoded PE unwind
ranges 0x14132f980..0x14133025e and 0x14132a8f0..0x14132b1ce. This is the direct
speaker role/description formatter. It calls the complete creature/profession
description supplier and appends native office, affiliation and curse identity
fields; the explicit curse-name append is reference 0x14133019d / classic
0x14132b10d. Its curse-name data is a typed world field, not an arbitrary tail
guessed to be a profession from its English spelling.
CREATURE/PROFESSION DESCRIPTION: reference-132e0c0.c / classic-1329030.c, independent
owners 0x14132e0c0..0x14132e428 and 0x141329030..0x141329398. These compose complete
creature/caste and profession strings and call the native profession-label
supplier at reference 0x14132cc10 / classic 0x141327b80, also exported here as
reference-132cc10.c / classic-1327b80.c. Native dispatch and complete RAW/custom
profession data select the role phrase; dynamically supplied role names remain
open fields, not a finite suffix spelling heuristic.
ALTERNATE UNIT CAPTION: reference-1331500.c / classic-132c470.c retain another
complete unit-reference constructor. The earlier unit-profession-caption label
for this owner was imprecise; it is not the direct role formatter above.
APPEARANCE: reference-717d30.c / classic-715750.c, with size construction in
reference-716b70.c / classic-714590.c. These supply the creature's complete native
descriptive phrase before the battle sentence is assembled.
SPEAKER: reference-1330c30.c / classic-132bba0.c. Native identity visibility and
name/profession formatting select the complete speaker caption.
SPEECH WRAPPER: reference-684a10.c / classic-682430.c. Complete speaker is replaced
by You for the adventure player; an addressed unit can add " (to " + SPEAKER +
")". A nonempty speaker caption adds ": ", then the complete supplied speech
body is appended. Missing speaker permits the speech body without that prefix.
One companion direct production is UNIT + " stops and pays attention to you.".
SPEECH TRANSFORM: reference-67b6c0.c / classic-6790e0.c. A caste-selected speech
branch processes S/s through temporary ([LIP])/([lip]) markers, then expands the
marked sounds; the body can consequently differ from its original literal text.
The speech body itself is an input to the wrapper, not a closed list of English
literals inside that wrapper. All finite upstream dialogue productions belong
to their native producer sources; world names, authored speech and future RAW
content within them remain open fields and must not be represented as an
exhaustive literal word list.

Complete adjacent producer trees and source correspondence
---------------------------------------------------------
data/extracted/announcement-conversation/decompiled-spoken-popup-source.txt
documents the complete speech wrapper, topic dispatcher, incident/memory types
and dynamic suppliers. Its native-role-correspondence.tsv links all 42 existing
ELF Ghidra C owner sources to the current reference and classic PE ranges and
their full original instruction bodies. reference-functions.tsv and
classic-functions.tsv retain 58 PE owners per image, including small leaf
suppliers without unwind metadata. PE instruction/source reconstructions in
that directory must not be mislabeled as Ghidra PE C: the 42 elf-<role>.c files
are actual ELF decompiler exports, while this combat directory now additionally
retains actual current-PE C for the shared speech wrapper and its field suppliers.

This task reran tools/extract_announcement_memory_pe.py against both configured
PEs. The conversation directory's reference-switches.tsv and classic-switches.tsv
each retain 5,102 native selector/target entries, including aliases, remaps and
default paths from the full retained source owners. reference-topic-dispatch.tsv
and classic-topic-dispatch.tsv retain every main conversation topic 0..253.
Those are source selector records, not a count of distinct sentences or a claim
that arbitrary generated text has been reduced to a finite list.

data/extracted/adventure-announcement-native/native-functions.tsv and its
elf-source-<VA>.c files retain the full existing adventure producer and queue
tree; elf-producers.asm, elf-queue-submission.asm, native-submissions.tsv,
native-calls.tsv and native-switches.tsv preserve its direct submission sites,
typed suppliers and routing branches. Its decompiled-source.cpp explains the
whole-string queue and actor/recipient/body ownership of those sources. The
broader data/extracted/announcement-popup-native/decompiled-popup-source.txt
and native-production-catalog.tsv connect the Windows popup transport, report
storage, fixed producers and complete report renderer to that shared universe.
Together with combat/status/death sources, these cover the source families that
can coexist in this panel, rather than extracting only the two screenshot lines.

Attack-record producer 0x14064a350..0x1406536b2
----------------------------------------------
Normal item attack obtains attack definitions from virtual item+0x438.
An attack definition stores base verb at +0x10, third-person verb at +0x30 and
weapon subpart at +0x50. The native producer copies those complete string fields
at 0x14064ae64..0x14064ae9b. Adventure player selects base, all other actors select
third-person at 0x14064af2d..0x14064af54. Missing/invalid item attack definition
selects literal strike/strikes (0x14064af07..0x14064af28). Projectile setup initially
assigns strikes (0x14064a9e6). A special shove uses push/pushes (0x14064b97a).
Creature attack paths obtain the corresponding complete RAW ATTACK_VERB fields.
The stealth branch prefixes "silently " to the already selected attack verb
(0x140650ebe..0x140650ef5); it does not alter the actor's identity.

INSTRUMENT = ["the " + complete SUBPART + " of "] + POSSESSIVE + " " + ITEM,
             or POSSESSIVE + " " + complete anatomical instrument BODY.
SUBPART is omitted when empty or equal to NO_SUB (0x14064af6a..0x14064af8f).
For a present subpart, 0x14064af91..0x14064afc5 appends the/of wrapper; it does
not constrain subpart to shaft, pommel or flat. PLAYER POSSESSIVE is your;
other actors use native sex-based possessive pronoun (0x14064afdc..0x14064b034).
ITEM is appended whole at 0x14064b063 with caption detail argument false.
The body instrument alternative at 0x14064b736..0x14064b7b3 uses the same ownership.

ACTOR = UNIT for a creature actor; this attack producer's projectile actor is
        "The flying " + ITEM / "The spinning " + ITEM.
The virtual flying predicate and projectile item kinds 0x27/0x41 choose flying;
the other branch chooses spinning (0x14064a82a..0x14064a8eb). The shared-damage
constructor independently also admits "The " + ITEM when its projectile flags
omit motion (0x1400e5887..0x1400e5951); that is not a third evasion-head branch.

TARGET_PRONOUN = You for the adventure player, otherwise He / She / It selected
from target.sex at +0x12e, with capitalization enabled. The target's full UNIT
caption and this grammatical subject pronoun are separate native strings.
The producer builds UNIT at 0x14064a90a and TARGET_PRONOUN at
0x14064a981 / 0x14064a995; independently configured classic calls are
0x14064832a and 0x1406483a1 / 0x1406483b5. The complete native helper is
0x140aa4730..0x140aa47a4 / 0x140aa17b0..0x140aa1824 and is retained as real
per-edition C and .asm in announcement-conversation/*-subject-pronoun.*.
Its finite selector is sex==1 -> he, sex==0 -> she, otherwise it; the last
argument capitalizes the first byte. You bypasses that helper. No unit name,
profession or arbitrary sentence tail is passed to this pronoun supplier.

Every finite direct sentence family of this producer:
  UNIT + " has moved out of range!"                 0x14064a578
  UNIT + (" let" | " lets") + " the " + BODY +
      " drop away as " + UNIT + (" attack." | " attacks.")
                                                   0x14064bb11..0x14064bbed
  UNIT + (" catch " | " catches ") + OWNED_BODY +
      " with " + OWNED_BODY + "!"                 0x14064bfe9..0x14064c33c
  ACTOR + (" attack " | " attacks ") + UNIT + " but " + EVASION + "!"
                                                   0x14064d2f8..0x14064d7c5,
                                                   0x14064e2ba..0x14064e3b1
  EVASION = TARGET_PRONOUN + (" scramble" | " scrambles" | " roll" | " rolls" |
                              " jump" | " jumps") + " away"
  UNIT + (" scramble" | " scrambles" | " roll" | " rolls" |
          " jump" | " jumps") + " away from " + ACTOR + "!"
                                                   0x14064e08a..0x14064e112
  ACTOR + (" miss " | " misses ") + UNIT + "!"  0x14064e61b..0x14064e658
  ACTOR + (" miss " | " misses ") + UNIT +
      " badly, blocked by the divine intervention of mighty " + DEITY + "!"
                                                   0x140650242..0x1406502c4
  SHOT + " but the shot is blocked!"              0x14064d55c
  SHOT + " but the shot is blocked" + [" with " + ITEM] + "!"
                                                   0x14064f1e4..0x14064f254
  SHOT + " but the shot is " + [PARRY_ADVERB] + "parried" +
      [" by " + ITEM] + "!"                      0x14064db47..0x14064dc18
  SHOT + " but the shot is " + [DEFLECT_ADVERB] + "deflected" +
      [" by " + ITEM] + "!"                      0x14064f933..0x14064fa0c
  SHOT = ACTOR + (" strike at " | " strikes at ") + UNIT
  PARRY_ADVERB = "deftly " | "just barely " | "easily " | empty
  DEFLECT_ADVERB = "effortlessly " | "narrowly " | "easily " | empty
  UNIT + (" block " | " blocks ") + ACTOR + [" with " + ITEM] + "!"
                                                   0x14064f299..0x14064f325
  UNIT + (" bat " | " bats ") + ACTOR + (" aside" | " out of the air") +
      [" with " + ITEM] + "!"                    0x14064fa4c..0x14064faf9
  UNIT_LIST + (" are " | " is ") + "stunned by divine power!"
                                                   0x140650b9e..0x140650c9a
  "Many are stunned by divine power!"             0x140650b5d..0x140650c9a
  UNIT_LIST preserves every selected unit with comma, comma-and, or and joining.
  UNIT + (" have" | " has") + " become enraged!" 0x14065336e..0x14065340f

The weapon optional clauses are omitted on null item pointer paths. Actor,
defender, projectile and equipment retain distinct typed ownership.
No adverb branch is a generalized global word replacement.

Both compound evasion sites append the capitalized TARGET_PRONOUN verbatim
after the lowercase connector " but ": 0x14064d327..0x14064d348 and
0x14064e2e9..0x14064e30a. Thus "but She jumps away!", "but He rolls away!"
and "but It scrambles away!" are the actual native spelling, including that
interior uppercase letter. Replacing these pronouns with the preceding full
unit caption would alter the native construction and misses the source field.
These two complete branches both choose the motion verb from the same finite
decision tree: target flags1 bit0x8000 clear -> jump/jumps; bit set -> random
two-way roll/rolls or scramble/scrambles. The adventure player alone uses the
base form; other targets use third-person, independently of the attacker.
The second branch's complete sources are 0x14064e30f..0x14064e3c4 (classic
0x14064bd2f..0x14064bde4); the first has split native basic blocks at
0x14064d34d..0x14064d391 and 0x14064d759..0x14064d7d8 (classic
0x14064ad6d..0x14064adb1 and 0x14064b179..0x14064b1f8). All six finite
verb forms and all four subject alternatives belong to this complete source
tree; they are not six screenshot-specific replacements. The projectile
variant instead starts with the complete target UNIT and appends the motion
plus " away from " + ACTOR + "!" (0x14064e051..0x14064e125 / classic
0x14064ba71..0x14064bb45), with no separate subject-pronoun substitution.

Additional complete prefixes passed through shared damage (record flag0x20):
  "The force bends the " + BODY                  0x1406530ad
  "The force twists the " + BODY                 0x1406530d8
  "The force pulls the " + BODY                  0x140653106
The three prefixes are stored in the damage record at 0x14065317d..0x1406531b1
and submitted to shared damage at 0x1406531ef, preserving every suffix family.

Wrestling producer 0x140646f00..0x14064a348
----------------------------------------
Subject inflection selects base for the adventure player and third-person for
other units. OWNED_BODY always contains owner plus the complete anatomical part.
Finite direct productions, with their original punctuation:
  UNIT + (" lock " | " locks ") + OWNED_BODY + " with " + OWNED_BODY + "!"
                                                   0x140647499..0x140647576
  UNIT + (" place" | " places") + " a chokehold on " + OWNED_BODY +
      " with " + OWNED_BODY + "!"               0x140647671..0x140647733
  UNIT + (" take " | " takes ") + UNIT + " down by the " + BODY +
      " with " + OWNED_BODY + "!"               0x140647850..0x140647912
  UNIT + (" throw " | " throws ") + UNIT + " by the " + BODY +
      " with " + OWNED_BODY + "!"               0x1406479f1..0x140647ab3
  UNIT + (" adjust" | " adjusts") + " the grip of " + OWNED_BODY +
      " on " + OWNED_BODY + "."                0x14064828d..0x14064834f
  UNIT + (" struggle" | " struggles") + " in vain against the grip of " +
      OWNED_BODY + " on " + OWNED_BODY + "."    0x1406486d2..0x140648794
  UNIT + (" release" | " releases" | " loosen" | " loosens") +
      (" the choke hold of " | " the joint lock of ") + OWNED_BODY +
      " on " + OWNED_BODY + "."                0x140648861..0x140648bde
  UNIT + (" release" | " releases" | " break" | " breaks") +
      " the grip of " + OWNED_BODY + " on " + OWNED_BODY + "."
                                                   0x140648ca5..0x140648e04,
                                                   0x1406494fe..0x140649601
  "The " + BODY + " is ripped away and remains in " + OWNER +
      (" mouth!" | " grip!")                    0x140649254..0x1406492e0
  UNIT + (" lose" | " loses") + " hold of the " + BODY + "!"
                                                   0x1406493b9..0x140649409
  UNIT + (" pass" | " passes") + " out."       0x140649a0d..0x140649a37
  UNIT + (" miss " | " misses ") + UNIT + "!"  0x140649ea3..0x140649ed2
Release/loosen branches choose either ownership order from native hold records;
the full owned fields must be carried in the selected order.

Prefixes forwarded into every shared-damage outcome:
  UNIT + (" pinch " | " pinches ") + OWNED_BODY + " with " + OWNED_BODY
                                                   0x140647d60..0x140647e2e
  UNIT + (" gouge " | " gouges ") + OWNED_BODY + " with " + OWNED_BODY
                                                   0x140647fe8..0x1406480b6
  UNIT + (" bend " | " bends ") + OWNED_BODY + " with " + OWNED_BODY
                                                   0x140648491..0x14064855e
  UNIT + (" shake " | " shakes ") + UNIT + " around by the " + BODY
                                                   0x14064903d..0x1406490a0
  UNIT + (" strangle " | " strangles ") + OWNED_BODY
                                                   0x1406497b7..0x140649866
The separate grab/grabs branch 0x140649ccf..0x140649d41 populates the ordinary
attack-record verb/instrument and uses the same normal damage-head constructor.

Grip state producer 0x141361370..0x141362544
------------------------------------------
Two complete owner/body pairs are constructed from units/body records; empty
singular RAW vectors or invalid body index use body part, and the plural path
uses body parts. Player ownership is Your, otherwise complete UNIT + "'s".
Success and positive grip record+0x1e:
  UNIT + (" release" | " releases") + " the grip of " + OWNED_BODY_A +
      " from " + OWNED_BODY_B + "."             0x141361ed8..0x141361fb1
Success and nonpositive record+0x1e:
  UNIT + (" break" | " breaks") + " the grip of " + OWNED_BODY_B +
      " from " + OWNED_BODY_A + "!"             0x141361fd3..0x1413620ac
Failure (input success byte false at 0x141361e8e):
  UNIT + (" are unable to break" | " is unable to break") + " the grip of " +
      OWNED_BODY_B + " on " + OWNED_BODY_A + "!" 0x14136210e..0x1413621f7
The from/on relation and swapped owner order are distinct source branches.
For either owned field, item-id -1 selects the complete body-name branch.
A different item-id selects item lookup and complete-item-caption; a failed
lookup leaves that noun empty after its already constructed owner and space.
The paired units have already been found before this caption block, so this
null item branch does not remove either unit owner. It must not substitute a
guessed species, body part or item identity into that empty native field.

Embedded item producer 0x140643f70..0x140646e24
--------------------------------------------
  UNIT + (" pull" | " pulls") + " on the embedded " + ITEM + "."
                                                   0x140645253..0x14064543a
  UNIT + (" try" | " tries") + " to remove " + ITEM + "."
                                                   0x14064560f..0x1406457f8
Caption arguments false/-1 at 0x1406452a0 and the corresponding remove branch.
Terminal periods are inline stores 0x1406452e2 and 0x14064569d, not C strings.
Item-removal job 0x141397100..0x141397497:
  UNIT + " pulls out and " + ("drops" | "releases") + " " + ITEM + "."
                                                   0x141397273..0x141397332
Native item predicate 0x1413610f0 chooses drops/releases; the job does not choose
a base-person alternative, even though UNIT may itself be the player caption.

Collision/projectile movement and impact producers
-------------------------------------------------
Collision 0x140eadea0..0x140eb3ac4:
  UNIT + (" skip" | " skips") + " across the " +
      ("water" | "magma" | "lava") + "!"      0x140eae9d7..0x140eaea96
  UNIT + (" slam" | " slams") + " into an obstacle!"
                                                   0x140eaf64e..0x140eaf67c,
                                                   0x140eb38a9..0x140eb38d6
  UNIT + (" slam" | " slams") + " into an obstacle and " +
      ("blow" | "blows") + " apart!"           0x140eaf3e1..0x140eaf46e,
                                                   0x140eb368b..0x140eb3711
  UNIT + (" slam" | " slams") + " into " + UNIT + "!"
                                                   0x140eb0235..0x140eb02e5,
                                                   0x140eb1c83..0x140eb1d2e,
                                                   0x140eb2f8a..0x140eb3044
  UNIT + (" scramble" | " scrambles" | " roll" | " rolls" |
          " jump" | " jumps") + " out of " + OWNER + " flight path!"
                                                   0x140eb1167..0x140eb12d6
Projectile movement 0x140ea8fb0..0x140eade98:
  UNIT + (" scramble" | " scrambles" | " roll" | " rolls" |
          " jump" | " jumps") + " away from the " + ITEM + "!"
                                                   0x140eab966..0x140eabb6e
Projectile motion invokes normal attack producer at 0x140eaab49, 0x140eac4b6,
0x140ead66b, 0x140ead79b and 0x140eadb1b. Collision similarly invokes it at
0x140eafda0 and 0x140eb0760, and invokes bodily impact for obstacle damage.

Bodily impact 0x1413b1580..0x1413b209d, positive force only:
  PREFIX = OWNER + " " + INLINE_BODY + " takes the full force of the impact"
                                                   0x1413b1b72
Ground skid 0x1413b20a0..0x1413b2a26, positive force only:
  PREFIX = OWNER + " " + INLINE_BODY + " skids along the ground"
                                                   0x1413b25b8
INLINE_BODY = singular RAW name for count<=1, plural RAW name for count>1,
body part for invalid body index, or body part/body parts for absent RAW names.
The native verbs remain takes/skids even when the selected RAW name is plural.
Both producers copy the COMPLETE prefix to record.kind0x12 with flag0x20, then
invoke shared damage: 0x1413b1cdc and 0x1413b2725. Thus skidding is a separate
prefix family composing with all damage suffixes, not a standalone status word.

Fire, web and material emission
------------------------------
0x1413650e0..0x1413654b6 breath defense:
  UNIT + (" block" | " blocks") +
      (" the fire." | " the dragonfire." | " the breath.")
enum input 0=fire, 1=dragonfire, 2=breath at 0x1413652ff..0x14136533f;
out-of-range enum submits only UNIT + block/blocks, with no object/punctuation.
0x1413654c0..0x141365983 and 0x141366000..0x1413664c6:
  UNIT + (" breathe" | " breathes") + " fire!"
0x141365990..0x141365ffa:
  UNIT + (" hurl" | " hurls") + " a ball of fire!"
0x1413664d0..0x141366854:
  UNIT + (" shoot" | " shoots") + " out thick strands of webbing!"
0x1413c72b0, 0x1413c8f60, 0x1413c9ad0, 0x1413ca1d0:
  UNIT + (" breathe" | " breathes") + " a cloud of " + MATERIAL + "!"
0x1413c80b0:
  UNIT + (" breathe" | " breathes") + " a glob of " + MATERIAL + "!"
Cloud/glob material can be builtin, plant, creature-owned or historical-creature
material; failed material resolution uses literal unknown material. The vapor
state appends " vapor". Native owner + "'s " and complete material name stay one
typed MATERIAL phrase. Source operands include these alternatives, not just fire.

Material ownership has three distinct native constructions:
  MATERIAL = complete RAW material/state name, with any complete material prefix;
  MATERIAL = (complete RAW species name | historical/assumed identity name) +
             "'s " + complete RAW material/state name;
  MATERIAL = "'s " + complete RAW material/state name, when the selected native
             identity has no name. This last construction is an actual source
             branch, not an empty translated capture or a guessed owner.
An absent material lookup may substitute unknown material in those same fields;
the vapor-state branch appends " vapor" after the full owned or owner-free field.

The empty-identity branch follows the native string construction directly:
0x1413c7525..0x1413c753d initializes the temporary name to an empty string;
0x1413c7541..0x1413c7579 selects assumed identity or the historical figure name.
At 0x1413c7582, name.has_name(+0x72)==false jumps to 0x1413c75a2 and skips the
name formatter. 0x1413c75a2..0x1413c75b6 nevertheless appends the still-empty
temporary string. 0x1413c75c1..0x1413c75cc then unconditionally appends "'s ".
Thus the owner bytes are exactly "'s ", and the subsequently appended complete
material produces actual "'s blood", "'s unknown material" or another RAW name.
Repeated identity blocks around 0x1413c7798 and 0x1413c79b8 have the same has_name
guard and unconditional apostrophe-s append. The glob producer repeats this at
0x1413c841c/0x1413c859e; the alternate cloud producer repeats it at 0x1413c923f,
0x1413c943c and 0x1413c965c. A real empty name must not be assigned an invented
species/identity or silently discarded during translation.

Vapor fallback append sequence is explicit: 0x1413c7886 selects "unknown material",
0x1413c7893..0x1413c7897 appends the selected material, and 0x1413c78a2 selects
" vapor" for the final append. The equivalent alternate cloud sites are
0x1413c94fb (unknown material) and 0x1413c9517 (vapor). Consequently the finite
fallbacks include "unknown material vapor" and "'s unknown material vapor",
as well as a named owner plus the complete material-vapor phrase.

Complete item caption with combat arguments
------------------------------------------
Logical owner 0x140c65450..0x140c65f0a; classic 0x140c62490..0x140c62f4a.
Combat instrument, projectile, object, blocking item, embedded item and removed
item call this function with detail argument r8b=false; count is -1 or 1.

if false && artifact reference exists && artifact.name_present(+0x7a):
    return language_name(artifact+0x8);  // 0x140c654b9..0x140c654e2
    // The result is a BARE generated artifact name, with no material/type.
if false && item_type==0x59 && nonempty item title(+0xe8):
    return complete_title + " (copy)"; // 0x140c654fc..0x140c65513
if false && item_type==0x56 && written content/improvement has nonempty title:
    return complete_written_title + " (copy)";
    // 0x140c65521..0x140c656f4; improvement kinds0xc/0x9; failed/empty lookup
    // falls through to ordinary subtype caption, rather than inventing a title.
ordinary:
    construct virtual article-title(+0x5f0, count), quality/improvement markers,
    wear wrappers, native ownership/magic marks and virtual full title(+0x5e8).
    // All 98 item owner methods and type/material/RAW suppliers are preserved
    // by data/extracted/item-description-sources.tsv. Specialized book, cage,
    // slab, statue/figurine, food, corpse and tool captions enter those methods.
    // Custom named cages/designations are authored fields, not adjective lists.
    // Artifact-name and written-title early returns bypass the ordinary title.
The shot block/parry/deflection sites pass count=1 to this entire supplier:
reference 0x14064dbf3, 0x14064f22f, 0x14064f300, 0x14064f9e7,
0x14064fad4; their classic counterparts are retained independently in the
classic-647d70 C/assembly and native-calls.tsv. The article is outside the
paired quality/designation span. A combat item's strict leaf must consume
that article and the complete marked noun together; matching a bare ::items
noun alone does not cover this producer. The scoped $combat-item path reuses
translate_inventory_item_name, which owns the same native article, decimal
suffix and designation grammar, then the existing announcement item grammar.
Anatomical equipment and all five possessive pronouns plus named-owner 's
remain separate equipment/owner branches before that item leaf.
All native shot-result literals remain semantic syntax: parried/deflected,
their respective finite adverbs, blocked, strike/strikes at, and the optional
by/with equipment clauses. Display composition may preserve an unknown typed
item or person field, but it cannot preserve a whole unresolved SHOT,
SHOT_RESULT, attack, evasion, damage or injury clause as an opaque name.
Quality/wear wrappers are whole item decorations, not ownership delimiters.
The finite dispatch branches are unchanged when an arbitrary item is wielded as
an improvised weapon; translating only material/type nouns omits bare names.

Corpse, body and material field suppliers
---------------------------------------
The current PE extraction additionally retains the complete corpse item virtual
methods, not just literals found in the report constructor:
  full body-component caption: 0x140ca1aa0 / 0x140c9eae0
  short body-component caption:0x140ca10e0 / 0x140c9e120
  body-component article:      0x140ca0d60 / 0x140c9dda0
  generic type/material noun:  0x140a82c10 / 0x140a7fc90
  complete body-name supplier: 0x1413345d0 / 0x14132f540
  material/state supplier:     0x1414d1920 / 0x1414cc890
All six have per-edition .asm and real Ghidra C here, together with their own
unwind ranges, finite operands, calls, conditions and selector destinations.
The classic corpse short method is read directly from item_corpsest vtable
0x1416436a8 +0x5f8; the full/article slots +0x5e8/+0x5f0 supply the two other
methods above. These are independent original-PE operands, not a global assumed
reference/classic address delta.

The full caption chooses player "your ", named live owner plus "'s ", named
historical figure plus "'s ", or the unnamed complete creature/caste label.
The two possessive branches call the pure language_name formatter a94030 on
unit+8 (ca1bfc) or historical figure+0x38 (ca1cb7), then append the possessive
at ca1c21/ca1cdc. They do not supply an actor/profession caption. A preceding
announcement action therefore cannot become an occupation inside this owner.
It then composes optional "rotten ", optional "mangled ", the selected body or
tissue/material field, and the finite body states skeleton, partial remains,
mutilated corpse, corpse. Partial skeleton/body states and optional [amount]
are retained in the native body-status branches. Short captions keep their own
"partial " path and number selection. Detached body components can combine a
complete body name, a material/state name, or the literal material fallback;
they are not only the finite corpse/skeleton nouns. The article supplier emits
no article for player/named owners; otherwise count==1 selects "the ", count==0
can select "a " for an unstacked single item, and other count/mass branches omit
the article. An open RAW creature/caste caption can itself contain generated
world-language words. Therefore a leading the/a is a separate native article,
not evidence that the following complete creature name is an authored alias.

World-generated creature labels are identified by the native RAW field rather
than by their spelling or article. data/upstream/df-structures/df.creature.xml
declares creature_raw_flags.GENERATED at zero-based index 91 and binds that enum
to creature_raw.flags. The active edition's native field bindings retain its
dynamic byte-array flags and the creature/caste name, baby and child arrays.
The render-side source snapshot publishes complete labels only for GENERATED
RAWs. Semantic creature translations precede phonetic rendering of a complete
generated name; personal owners and authored nicknames keep their separate
language_name/identity paths. Stored body captions use the same typed grammar
as live animation labels, including all status, component and quantity fields.

The body-name method selects RAW singular/plural and INDIVIDUAL_NAME according
to requested index, count mode and body count; missing/invalid data emits body
part or body parts, optionally with the native numeric prefix. Material-state
selection retains category flags, historical-figure-associated material names,
RAW state names and the exact unknown material fallback. These input namespaces
stay distinct from personal names and complete decorated item descriptions.

Shared damage and companion state/death source ownership
-------------------------------------------------------
0x1400e56a0..0x1400e9f40 is re-extracted here in reference-e56a0.asm and classic.
Its fully reconstructed production tree is recorded in
data/extracted/announcement-combat-status/decompiled-shared-damage.txt and
decompiled-productions.tsv: ordinary/prebuilt heads; flag0x4 by-the vs in-the;
flag0x8 item vs body; direction behind/side; optional complete instrument;
deflection, tapping, no-force, pass-through, glance-away, all destroyed-layer
outcomes, detached-part/torso outcomes, every damage verb and omitted-repeat-verb
list, hole/jamming/fraction/equipment/fluid suffix, artery/nerve/ligament/tendon
injury flag ordering, gelding, equipment break, interruption, rage, embedded
item, latching, propulsion, unconsciousness, repeated stun/breathing/sickness,
injected/poured/flowed/splattered/crumbled/sucked material and silent record cases.
These source records are shared by ordinary strikes, wrestling, collision,
full-impact, force bend/twist/pull and the newly identified ground-skid head.
The normal outcome also reaches the equipment append at 0x1400e82df when the
record count at context+0x4284 is zero, or when the retained records emit no
kind4/5 damage text. A failed kind5 damage-record lookup can break the loop
before its separator is appended. Thus H + " through the " + ITEM + "!" is a
complete native production without a preceding damage-list or comma. The
separate kind14 fluid loop at 0x1400e8351 may append repeated " and spilling "
+ FLUID after H or after that equipment suffix. Empty damage text does not
mean that the native head, equipment, fluid or final punctuation were omitted.
0x1400e9ecc is the 29-case aux dispatch; three preceding six-case injury tables
and unsigned-default branches are preserved in native-switches.tsv.
Null item lookup can leave the relation or deflection connector with no object;
optional item/prefix/body fields must retain that branch's ownership and spelling.

Companion status and death producers are separately extracted from both PEs in
data/extracted/announcement-status and data/extracted/fortress-missing-death.
Their status-update, state-helper, full unit/role/name suppliers and direct
submission paths include vomiting, recovery, pain/unconsciousness, hunger/thirst,
exposure, agitation/mood and death announcements that coexist with battle reports.
These finite native captions enter the existing announcement state grammar.

Installed RAW attack inputs
---------------------------
raw-attack-fields.tsv retains every ATTACK and ATTACK_VERB source token in both
configured games' vanilla and installed_mods object directories and available
mods object directories. raw-procedural-attack-sources.tsv retains every matching
installed vanilla Lua source expression; literal fields join the verb/part tables.
raw-source-roots.tsv records those source ownership classes: a file in mods is
an available candidate, not proof that it was loaded into the running world.
Current finite weapon subparts: flat, handle, helve, pommel, shaft. NO_SUB omits
the subpart construction entirely and is not displayed. Complete RAW verbs retain
both base and third-person forms in raw-attack-verbs.tsv. Additional jab/jabs come
from available Steam MOD 2925028826 (500502), item_extra_weapons.txt:152,164.
Unknown future RAW verbs/parts are dynamically supplied strings; spelling alone
does not provide translation or an identity-source classification.
